W3 (cost lens), after E012. The tip is E010. It runs Muon (3 Newton-Schulz steps), Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 at 40/30/30%, batch 2000, last group 512, 9.5 epochs in code (238 steps). It scores 6.64 s at 0.7548, only 0.18 pp above the 0.753 bar. E012 re-ran the tip and gave a bit-identical accuracy (0.754767) and a time within 0.1%. That confirms compiled runs are deterministic per seed and time noise is under 1%. The results table does not show E012's held-out seeds 3-12, so the 40-seed offset is still unknown.

Measured prices (time per pp of accuracy):
- Compile plus fused SGD: −14% time (E004). A recompile leak costs about +3 s (E003).
- Lookahead/EMA: about +1 pp at roughly zero time (E005).
- Muon: +0.66 pp for +4% time (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: −22% time for −0.59 pp (E007), about 3.5 s per pp. A good trade.
- Aggressive resizing (E011): about 0.9 s per pp. A bad trade. Accuracy loss turns super-linear once the 32 px tail is ≤20% or 20 px is used.
- Epochs: about 2 s per pp (E008).
- Width 576→512: about 1.6 s per pp (E010).
- LR decay to 0 on top of EMA: noise (E009).

Budget: time ≈ F + V × pixel fraction, with F about 0.5-0.8 s and V about 7.5 s at full resolution. Steps take ~26 ms each and GPU compute dominates. Launch and host overhead is probably 3-6% under the 4-CPU pin. The step has three compiled regions (fwd/bwd, Muon, fused SGD), Python-float LR writes and a Python Lookahead. That caps CUDA graphs or break removal at about 0.2-0.4 s, and both risk changing kernels, which reshuffles accuracy by ~0.2-0.3 pp.

Accuracy levers:
- Muon renormalizes filter norms every step, so weight decay only touches the BN biases, whitening bias and head. That makes the wd lever weak.
- Muon lr is the effective angular step size. The airbench value is probably near-optimal within ±0.3 pp.
- Plain EMA without the fast-weight reset is likely slightly worse than Lookahead: the alpha ramp ends near 0.77 per 5 steps, so it is only a short-horizon endpoint average.
- The real way to buy margin is epochs, at ~2 s per pp.

The tip is fragile. A negative 40-seed offset would force +0.25-0.5 epoch (+0.2-0.4 s).

Noise: per-seed std is about 0.2-0.35 pp, so the 3-seed SE is about 0.15-0.2 pp. Recipe reshuffles move the mean by up to ~0.3 pp. Time noise is about 1%.

Misses: I keep underestimating gains from known-good airbench components and the time saved by small resolutions. I overestimated the accuracy kept under aggressive resizing.

Unsure about:
- the 40-seed offset;
- the true launch-overhead fraction;
- whether CUDA-graph capture works with the separately compiled Muon and Lookahead steps without leaks.

forecasts.reason: Launch overhead is only ~3-6% of a GPU-bound step, so the gain is about 0.15-0.3 s, right at the 3% threshold. Capture complexity can leak or reshuffle kernels.
Muon lr is an angular step on norm-fixed filters. Airbench's 0.24 is probably near the flat optimum, so I expect within ±0.3 pp, i.e. noise.
Muon renormalizes the filters, so wd only touches the BN biases and head. It is a weak lever and the change will likely be under 0.3 pp.
The run is GPU-bound. Removing breaks and the Python-scalar LR likely saves under 3%, and folding augmentation into the compiled region may change the RNG stream.
The Lookahead pull toward the EMA also regularizes the trajectory. A plain short-horizon EMA likely loses about 0.2-0.4 pp and drops below the bar.

cruxes: What did E012 measure for the seeds 3-12 mean versus 0.7548? A negative offset forces buying about 0.3 pp back with epochs (+0.3 s) before any speed idea counts.
What is the measured GPU idle fraction per train step under the 4-CPU pin? Above 8% makes CUDA graphs and break removal worth about 0.4 s; below 4% makes them noise.
Is there any accuracy lever (BN recalibration, LS 0.2, Muon lr) worth at least 0.3 pp for free? That margin could fund a 0.5-epoch cut or a 24 px share above 40%, worth about 0.3-0.5 s.
